articles.full_text:
उत्तरी वियतनाम मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान केंद्र का पूर्वानुमान है कि 8 अगस्त की रात और 9 अगस्त के दिन हनोई में बादल छाए रहेंगे, रात में हल्की बारिश होगी, दिन में गर्म और धूप वाला मौसम रहेगा और उत्तर-पश्चिम दिशा से दूसरे स्तर की हवा चलेगी। शहर के केंद्र में अधिकतम तापमान 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा; उत्तरी, दक्षिणी और पश्चिमी क्षेत्रों में यह 34-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस होगा।
हनोई में कई दिनों तक चलने वाली भीषण गर्मी का दौर शुरू हो रहा है।
9 से 14 अगस्त तक हनोई में भीषण गर्मी रहेगी और अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 34-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा। 15 अगस्त से गर्मी धीरे-धीरे कम होने लगेगी और दोपहर और शाम के समय गरज के साथ बारिश की संभावना है।
9 अगस्त की रात और 10 अगस्त के दिन हनोई में बारिश नहीं हुई और मौसम सुहाना और धूपदार बना रहा। अधिकतम तापमान 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 26-29 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा।
एजेंसी का अनुमान है कि हनोई में यह भीषण गर्मी 14 अगस्त तक जारी रह सकती है। लंबे समय तक चलने वाली गर्मी से बिजली की मांग बढ़ जाती है, आग और विस्फोट का खतरा बढ़ जाता है, और जंगल में आग लगने का खतरा भी बढ़ जाता है; साथ ही, लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान के संपर्क में रहने वालों को निर्जलीकरण, थकावट और लू लगने जैसी समस्याएं भी हो सकती हैं।
जल विज्ञान की दृष्टि से, तुयेन क्वांग और होआ बिन्ह जलविद्युत जलाशयों में एक निचला जल निकासी द्वार खुला रखा गया है। रेड नदी और डुओंग नदी में जलस्तर में धीमी गति से गिरावट का अनुमान है; दा नदी में होआ बिन्ह जलाशय के नियमन के अनुसार उतार-चढ़ाव होगा, और डे नदी में ज्वार-भाटे के प्रभाव से धीमी गति से परिवर्तन होता रहेगा।
पूर्वी सागर में मौसम की बात करें तो, 8 अगस्त को दोपहर 1 बजे, उष्णकटिबंधीय निम्न दबाव का केंद्र हैनान द्वीप (चीन) के पश्चिम में स्थित था। इसकी अधिकतम हवा की गति स्तर 6 और झोंके स्तर 8 थे, और यह धीरे-धीरे पूर्व-दक्षिण-पूर्व दिशा में बढ़ रहा था। पूर्वानुमान है कि 9 अगस्त को सुबह 1 बजे तक, यह उष्णकटिबंधीय निम्न दबाव धीरे-धीरे कमजोर होकर निम्न दबाव क्षेत्र में बदल जाएगा। इस उष्णकटिबंधीय निम्न दबाव के तूफान में बदलने की संभावना नहीं है और यह वियतनाम में दस्तक नहीं देगा।

articles.full_text:
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, 8 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र, थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक का इलाका और पूर्वी क्वांग न्गाई में स्थानीय लू चली। दोपहर 1 बजे कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो गया, जैसे कि निम्नलिखित स्टेशनों पर: बाक मे (तुयेन क्वांग) 37.0 डिग्री, हुउ लुंग (लैंग सोन) 35.2 डिग्री, हिएप होआ ( बाक निन्ह ) 35.4 डिग्री, निन्ह बिन्ह 36.6 डिग्री, कोन कुओंग (न्घे आन) 36.4 डिग्री, बा तो (क्वांग न्गाई) 35.6 डिग्री, आदि; दोपहर 1 बजे सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 65-75% थी।
उत्तरी और मध्य वियतनाम में फैली भीषण गर्मी की लहर कितने समय तक चलेगी?
SKĐS - 9 अगस्त को वियतनाम के उत्तरपूर्वी क्षेत्र में भीषण गर्मी पड़ी, जहां अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहा और कुछ क्षेत्रों में 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो गया; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 60-65% थी। उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र, थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक का इलाका और क्वांग न्गाई के पूर्वी भाग में भी भीषण गर्मी रही, जहां तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर था।
9 अगस्त को वियतनाम के उत्तरपूर्वी क्षेत्र में भीषण गर्मी पड़ी, जहां अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहा और कुछ क्षेत्रों में 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो गया; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 60-65% थी। उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र, थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक का इलाका और पूर्वी क्वांग न्गाई में भी छिटपुट लू चली, जहां कुछ स्थानों पर अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो गया।
10 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र (लाई चाऊ, डिएन बिएन और उत्तरी सोन ला को छोड़कर), थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक का इलाका और पूर्वी क्वांग न्गाई में गर्म मौसम रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा, कुछ स्थानों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो सकता है; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 55-60% रहेगी।
14-15 अगस्त के दौरान उत्तरी क्षेत्र में लू धीरे-धीरे कम होने की संभावना है, जबकि मध्य क्षेत्र में लू जारी रहने की संभावना है। लू के कारण प्राकृतिक आपदा का खतरा स्तर 1 है।
तीव्र गर्मी और कम आर्द्रता के संयुक्त प्रभाव से, बिजली की बढ़ती मांग के कारण आवासीय क्षेत्रों में विस्फोट और आग लगने का खतरा बढ़ जाता है। इसके अलावा, लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान के संपर्क में रहने से निर्जलीकरण हो सकता है।
कृपया ध्यान दें कि लू की रिपोर्टों में तापमान का पूर्वानुमान और बाहर का वास्तविक तापमान कंक्रीट या डामर जैसी सतहों की स्थिति के आधार पर 1-3 डिग्री या उससे भी अधिक भिन्न हो सकता है।

South Korea braces for extreme heat as heat-related illnesses surge
Heavy rain expected in parts of east coast and mountainous areas of Gangwon province
Islamuddin Sajid
08 August 2026•Update: 08 August 2026
ISLAMABAD
Most parts of South Korea are facing an intense heat wave, with daytime temperatures forecast to reach as high as 37C (98.6F), local media reported Saturday, citing the state weather service.
The Korea Meteorological Administration forecast heavy rain of up to 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) in parts of the east coast and mountainous areas of Gangwon province Saturday afternoon, while Seoul and central regions could receive up to 40 mm of rain, according to Yonhap News Agency.
Temperatures may briefly fall during the rain but are expected to rise again as heat and humidity return.
Authorities have also temporarily reduced or suspended some driving tests because of concerns over heat-related illnesses.
Government data showed an annual average of 638 heat-related illness cases were reported from early August to the end of the month during 2021-2025, nearly three times the 2011-2015 average of 215.
In 2024, 1,299 people suffered heat-related illnesses during the period and 12 died.
Forecasters expect the heat wave to continue into late August, with daytime temperatures generally ranging between 31C (87.8F) and 35C (95F) across the country.

Study: Dutch spent less during extreme heat, especially outside of the major cities
Dutch households spent less money during the extreme heat in June, according to research by ABN Amro. Around that time, the KNMI issued its first-ever code red for heat. People do, however, spend more money at the supermarkets during the severe heat.
In the warm summer days leading up to the code red, people made ample use of outdoor terraces and other open-air activities. As a result, the number of pin payments rose just before the hottest days.
“The Dutch like to go out when the weather is nice,” ABN Amro economist and data scientist Jeannine van Reeken-Van Wee told NOS. “Only when temperatures become extreme do you see that people refrain from that.”
On the days when temperatures reached 39 degrees, the bank recorded both lower spending and fewer cash withdrawals.
The impact differed sharply between cities and rural areas. In cities, some people sought relief outdoors and headed to restaurants, cafes, and other venues away from home.
“Houses in the city often heat up faster, and people less often have a garden to sit in. They go to places to cool down and then spend money there,” Van Reeken explained.
In regional areas, the drop in spending was greater. One reason is that more older people live there. “The elderly are often more vulnerable and stay indoors more during extreme heat,” Van Reeken said. That pattern may also partly explain why fuel spending fell more sharply in more rural areas during the heat.
Supermarkets were the exception. Nationwide, grocery spending rose during the heat while pin payments at other stores fell.

Parts of Karnataka are being lashed with heavy to heavy rains on Saturday. The Indian Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for the entire state for both rains and strong surface winds.
An orange alert was issued for Dakshina Kannada, Shivamoga, and Chikkamagaluru, while a yellow alert was issued for Uttara Kannada, Kodagu and Udupi.
The Meteorological Department warned that there would be widespread rain in most parts of the state for about 12 hours on Saturday.
Heavy rains are likely to increase in the Coastal and Malnad regions.
The rains are to be accompanied by winds reaching speeds of 30 to 40 kmph.
In south interior Karnataka, heavy rains are forecast in Shivamogga and Chikkamagaluru,
Light to moderate rain, meanwhile, can be expected at Bengaluru Urban and Rural, Chamarajanagara, Chikkaballapura, Chitradurga, Davangere, Kolar, Mandya, Mysuru, Ramanagara, Tumakuru, Kodagu, Hassan and Vijayanagara.
The Dakshina Kannada district Disaster Management Authority has also declared a holiday for Anganwadi centres. All government, aided and private high schools and pre-university colleges in Puttut, Belthangady, Sulya and Kadaba Taluks.
Meanwhile, North Interior Karnataka is expected to receive lighter rainfall, with light to moderate rain at a few places over Belagavi, Gadag, Dharwad and Haveri, while light rain is likely over Bagalkot, Bidar, Kalaburagi, Koppal, Raichur, Vijayapura and Yadgir. Winds gusting at 40 to 50 kmph can also be expected in the parts of the region.
The rains can be expected to continue to next week. Most of the heavy rains in the state can be expected to be in the coastal parts.
Residents have also been advised to avoid low-lying areas, lakes, riverbanks and seashores.

Heavy rain brings Delhi to standstill, IMD issues red alert
Heavy rain brought large parts of the national capital to a standstill on Friday, submerging arterial roads under up to four feet of water, leaving vehicles stranded, choking traffic and inundating residential colonies as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert.
From the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road in south Delhi to Mahipalpur, Minto Road, ITO, Shakarpur and Chhatarpur, roads disappeared beneath rainwater as commuters remained trapped in traffic for hours, motorists abandoned flooded stretches and office-goers struggled to book cabs. Those who were able to leave for their home were stuck on the road as traffic congestion was reported from several important routes across Delhi, including Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, Wazirabad Road, Patel Road, Rohtak Road, Shankar Road, Laxmi Nagar, the Kirti Nagar stretch, the Delhi-Jaipur Highway, Peeragarhi, and Shaheen Bagh.
Delhi recorded its wettest first week of August since 2011, receiving 127 mm of rainfall during the first seven days of the month as relentless rain lashed the national capital through Friday. In several places in Delhi, the rainfall has crossed 100 mm. Pushp Vihar recorded 111.5 mm, Chhatarpur 104.5 mm and Ayanagar 87.4 mm rainfall till 5.30 pm. The city on Friday received its highest rainfall during the first week of August in 15 years, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Some of the worst flooding was reported on the Mehrauli-Badarpur (MB) Road near Vayusena Bad (Air Force Station), where water accumulated up to three to four feet deep, reducing one of south Delhi’s busiest corridors into what residents described as a river. Traffic crawled for kilometres between Khanpur and Okhla Mor, while adjoining stretches at Sangam Vihar, Deoli and Ambedkar Nagar also remained inundated. The downpour triggered a flood of civic complaints across the capital. Authorities received at least 67 rain-related complaints, including incidents of waterlogging, fallen trees and power outages. Delhi Fire Services (DFS) has received more than two dozen calls related to house collapses, portions of buildings giving way and fallen trees since midnight. However, no one was injured in these incidents.
According to the weather office, Pushp Vihar recorded the highest rainfall at 111.5 mm, followed by Chhatarpur (104.5 mm), Ayanagar (87.4 mm), Palam (73.5 mm), Janakpuri (68 mm), Jharoda Kalan (67 mm), Pusa (59.5 mm), Safdarjung (57.3 mm), Narayana (53 mm), Ridge (49.6 mm), Lodi Road (49.3 mm), Mayur Vihar (36 mm), Najafgarh (24 mm) and Jafarpur (13.5 mm) between 8.30 am and 5.30 pm. Delhi received 127 mm of rainfall during the first week of August, making it the wettest first week of the month since 2011. Rainfall was lighter across the Ghaziabad and Noida stations, at 13.5 mm and 11.5 mm, respectively.
Continuous rainfall led to severe waterlogging in several neighbourhoods, including areas around the Red Fort, Chhatarpur Farm, Mehram Nagar near Terminal 1 and Sainik Farms.
At Mahipalpur T-Point, waterlogging affected traffic heading towards the airport, Gurugram, Chhatarpur and Vasant Vihar, while commuters also reported long delays near the Pusa Road roundabout.
As rain continued to pour through the day, scenes from south Delhi’s Fatehpur Beri captured the scale of the disruption. In Valmiki Basti, while some residents waded through waist-deep water, the others carried schoolchildren across flooded lanes on a large blue plastic sheet used as a makeshift raft.
Severe waterlogging was also reported at the Delhi Police’s Narcotics office in south Delhi. In east Delhi’s Shakarpur and neighbouring Mandawali, e-rickshaw drivers said submerged potholes, overflowing drains and waterlogged roads had led to multiple accidents and sharply affected their earnings.
According to the MCD’s Central Control Room, tree-fall incidents were reported from the Keshavpuram, South, Central, West and Civil Lines zones. The NDMC received 34 rain-related complaints, including 15 cases of waterlogging, five tree-fall incidents and 14 power outages, while the PWD logged 22 complaints of waterlogging.
Waterlogging complaints in the NDMC area were reported from Lodhi Road, Sunehari Bagh Road, RK Ashram Marg, Minto Road Bridge, Rajiv Chowk Metro, Safdarjung Flyover, Lady Hardinge Medical College, Moti Bagh, Talkatora Garden, Race Course Road and Sarojini Nagar. Tree-fall incidents were reported from Lady Hardinge Medical College, Yashwant Place in Chanakyapuri, RML Hospital and Jam Nagar House.
The heavy rain also triggered political sparring, with the Delhi Congress blaming the BJP-led Centre, the Delhi government and the MCD for the widespread flooding. Senior Congress leader and former MLA Mukesh Sharma alleged that desilting of drains existed only on paper and said the “triple-engine government” had failed to prevent waterlogging despite repeated assurances.
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), in a post on X, said the BJP “never tires of taking credit” for resolving waterlogging at Minto Bridge while ignoring flooding elsewhere in the city. There was no immediate statement from the Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government on the opposition’s allegations.

Red alert issued for severe mountain floods in Zhejiang
The Ministry of Water Resources and the China Meteorological Administration on Saturday jointly issued a red alert for mountain flood risks, warning of possible severe flooding in parts of East China's Zhejiang province.
According to a statement released by the Ministry of Water Resources on its official WeChat account, the alert is effective from 8 pm Saturday to 8 pm Sunday.
During this period, some areas in eastern Zhejiang are expected to face a high risk of mountain floods, with localized areas facing an extremely higher risk, according to the alert. An orange alert has been issued for areas with a high possibility of mountain floods, while a red alert has been issued for regions where such disasters are highly likely.
Other regions may also experience mountain floods triggered by short-duration intense rainfall, the alert said.
Authorities have urged local governments in affected areas to strengthen real-time monitoring, improve flood prevention warnings and take timely measures, including organizing evacuations to ensure people's safety.
